questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to give blood safely at a hospital or clinic
Why Japanese popstars share their personal details
Blood types: beliefs about personality and real uses
How the immune system fights viruses like the flu
questions.why: They find out why humans have different blood types and whether blood is more than a way to carry oxygen.

questions.q: What does Neil admit about his blood type?
options: He doesn't know it
He is type O like Sam
He has a very rare type
He is type A

questions.q: According to Sam, how are blood groups used in parts of Asia?
options: To decide who can get a job in a big company
Only for keeping medical records up to date
To choose which school children should attend
To choose partners and describe personality
questions.why: Sam says people select partners based on blood type and link blood groups to personalities.

questions.q: How does Chie Kobayashi describe typical type A people?
options: Creative, independent and happy to work alone
Perfectionists, good at teamwork, who follow rules
Curious, stubborn and generous with their money
Selfish, lazy and quite hard to work with
questions.why: She says type As are perfectionists, detail-oriented, good at teamwork and respecting rules.

questions.q: Roughly what percentage of Japan's population is type A, according to Marnie Chesterton?
options: 10 percent
20 percent
40 percent
30 percent
questions.why: She says 40 percent of Japan's population are sensitive, anxious type As.

questions.q: What is Dr Emma Pomeroy's view of blood types and personality?
options: There is no scientific link, as with horoscopes
The link is strong, but only for people in Japan
Scientists have now proved the link in many studies
The link is true for people with type B blood only
questions.why: She thinks that, like horoscopes, there's no scientific basis for a connection.

questions.q: What do blood types actually do in the body?
options: Decide how much oxygen the blood can carry
Control a person's mood and level of energy
Make the blood thicker or thinner in the veins
Act as markers that help the body spot pathogens
questions.why: Sam says they are chemical markers which support the immune system and identify pathogens.

questions.q: Why is type O blood in high demand?
options: It is the rarest type
It can be given to anyone
It protects against all diseases
Most people in Japan are type O
questions.why: Neil mentions the high demand for type O blood, which can be given to anyone.
